blocks.content: Compose automatically creates a dedicated network for your project, every service joins it by default, which is exactly what makes services able to reach each other by name without any manual network setup.

Without any networks configuration at all, Compose still creates one project-specific network and attaches every service to it, this is not something you have to set up yourself, it happens the moment you run docker compose up.

blocks.alt: A default network, created and attached automatically

blocks.content: 2. Name-Based Resolution, Out of the Box
blocks.text: 2. Name-Based Resolution, Out of the Box

blocks.content: Because that default network is a custom (user-defined) network under the hood, it comes with the automatic DNS-by-name resolution covered in the Docker Networking module, an app service connecting to db just works, no IP addresses, no manual linking.

blocks.alt: Every service can reach every other service, by name, automatically

blocks.content: For more deliberate topology, a top-level networks block can define additional networks beyond the automatic default, giving you explicit control over which services can reach which others.

blocks.alt: Extra networks, declared explicitly when the default is not enough

blocks.content:
services:
  web:
    networks: [frontend]
  db:
    networks: [backend]
networks:
  frontend:
  backend:

code.content:
services:
  web:
    networks: [frontend]
  db:
    networks: [backend]
networks:
  frontend:
  backend:

codes.yaml:
services:
  web:
    networks: [frontend]
  db:
    networks: [backend]
networks:
  frontend:
  backend:

blocks.content: Assigning services to different custom networks keeps them genuinely unable to reach each other, useful for a real security boundary, a public-facing web service and an internal database can be kept apart even within the same Compose stack, if that separation matters for your setup.

blocks.alt: Services split across networks stay genuinely isolated from each other

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Compose creates a default project network automatically, every service joins it and can reach every other service by name, with zero manual setup.
A top-level networks block lets you define additional, more deliberately isolated networks when the automatic default is not granular enough.
